questions.text: Let $f(x)=\log_e x$ and $g(x)=\dfrac{x^4-2x^3+3x^2-2x+2}{2x^2-2x+1}$. Then the domain of $fog$ is
questions.sol:
$f\circ g$ needs $g(x)>0$.
Denominator: $2x^2-2x+1=x^2+(x-1)^2>0$ for every $x$.
Numerator: $x^4-2x^3+3x^2-2x+2=(x^2-x)^2+2(x^2-x+1)>0$, since $x^2-x+1>0$ always.
So $g(x)>0$ for all real $x$ and the domain is $\mathbb{R}$.

questions.text: Let $R=\{(1,2),(2,3),(3,3)\}$ be a relation defined on the set $\{1,2,3,4\}$. Then the minimum number of elements, needed to be added in $R$ so that $R$ becomes an equivalence relation, is:
questions.sol:
Since $1R2$ and $2R3$, transitivity and symmetry force $1,2,3$ into one class, so all 9 pairs of $\{1,2,3\}\times\{1,2,3\}$ are needed; 4 needs only $(4,4)$.
The smallest equivalence relation has $9+1=10$ pairs.
$R$ already has 3 of them, so $10-3=7$ must be added: $(1,1),(2,2),(2,1),(3,2),(1,3),(3,1),(4,4)$.

questions.text: Let $\left|\dfrac{\bar z-i}{2\bar z+i}\right|=\dfrac13$, $z\in\mathbb{C}$, be the equation of a circle with center at C. If the area of the triangle, whose vertices are at the points $(0,0)$, C and $(\alpha,0)$ is 11 square units, then $\alpha^2$ equals:
questions.sol:
Let $\bar z=x+iy$. Then $9|\bar z-i|^2=|2\bar z+i|^2$:
$9\left(x^2+(y-1)^2\right)=4x^2+(2y+1)^2 \Rightarrow 5x^2+5y^2-22y+8=0$.
So $\bar z$ lies on a circle with centre $\left(0,\dfrac{11}{5}\right)$; $z$ is its mirror image in the real axis, so C $=\left(0,-\dfrac{11}{5}\right)$.
Area $=\dfrac12\cdot|\alpha|\cdot\dfrac{11}{5}=11 \Rightarrow |\alpha|=10$, so $\alpha^2=100$.

questions.text:
If the system of equations
$(\lambda-1)x+(\lambda-4)y+\lambda z=5$
$\lambda x+(\lambda-1)y+(\lambda-4)z=7$
$(\lambda+1)x+(\lambda+2)y-(\lambda+2)z=9$
has infinitely many solutions, then $\lambda^2+\lambda$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Expanding the coefficient determinant gives $\Delta=-4\lambda^2+10\lambda+6=-2(2\lambda+1)(\lambda-3)$, so $\Delta=0$ for $\lambda=3$ or $-\dfrac12$.
For $\lambda=3$: $2x-y+3z=5$, $3x+2y-z=7$, $4x+5y-5z=9$. The third equation is $-1\times$(first) $+\,2\times$(second), right-hand side included ($-5+14=9$), so there are infinitely many solutions.
$\lambda^2+\lambda=9+3=12$ (the other root gives $-\dfrac14$, not an option).

questions.text: If A, B, and $(\operatorname{adj}(A^{-1})+\operatorname{adj}(B^{-1}))$ are non-singular matrices of same order, then the inverse of $A(\operatorname{adj}(A^{-1})+\operatorname{adj}(B^{-1}))^{-1}B$, is equal to
questions.sol:
The inverse is $B^{-1}\left(\operatorname{adj}(A^{-1})+\operatorname{adj}(B^{-1})\right)A^{-1}$.
$\operatorname{adj}(A^{-1})=|A^{-1}|\,(A^{-1})^{-1}=\dfrac{A}{|A|}$, and similarly for $B$.
So the inverse is $B^{-1}\dfrac{A}{|A|}A^{-1}+B^{-1}\dfrac{B}{|B|}A^{-1}=\dfrac{B^{-1}}{|A|}+\dfrac{A^{-1}}{|B|}$.
With $B^{-1}=\dfrac{\operatorname{adj}B}{|B|}$ and $A^{-1}=\dfrac{\operatorname{adj}A}{|A|}$ this is $\dfrac{1}{|AB|}(\operatorname{adj}B+\operatorname{adj}A)$.

questions.text: The number of words, which can be formed using all the letters of the word "DAUGHTER", so that all the vowels never come together, is
questions.sol:
DAUGHTER has 8 different letters, with vowels A, U, E.
All arrangements: $8!=40320$.
Vowels together (treat them as one block): $6!\times3!=4320$.
Vowels not all together: $40320-4320=36000$.

questions.text: One die has two faces marked 1, two faces marked 2, one face marked 3 and one face marked 4. Another die has one face marked 1, two faces marked 2, two faces marked 3 and one face marked 4. The probability of getting the sum of numbers to be 4 or 5, when both the dice are thrown together, is
questions.sol:
Count the 36 equally likely face pairs.
Sum 4: (1,3) $2\times2=4$, (2,2) $2\times2=4$, (3,1) $1\times1=1$: 9 ways.
Sum 5: (1,4) $2\times1=2$, (2,3) $2\times2=4$, (3,2) $1\times2=2$, (4,1) $1\times1=1$: 9 ways.
Probability $=\dfrac{18}{36}=\dfrac12$.

questions.text: Let the area of a $\Delta$PQR with vertices P(5, 4), Q($-2$, 4) and R(a, b) be 35 square units. If its orthocenter and centroid are $\mathrm{O}\left(2,\dfrac{14}{5}\right)$ and C(c, d) respectively, then $c+2d$ is equal to
questions.sol:
PQ lies on $y=4$, so the altitude from R is vertical and passes through O: $a=2$.
The altitude from P is perpendicular to QR $=(4,\,b-4)$ and passes through O: $(2-5)\cdot4+\left(\dfrac{14}{5}-4\right)(b-4)=0 \Rightarrow b-4=-10$, so $b=-6$ (the area is then $\dfrac12\cdot7\cdot10=35$, as required).
Centroid: $c=\dfrac{5-2+2}{3}=\dfrac53$, $d=\dfrac{4+4-6}{3}=\dfrac23$.
$c+2d=\dfrac53+\dfrac43=3$.

questions.text: If $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\le x\le\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$, then $\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{12}{13}\cos x+\dfrac{5}{13}\sin x\right)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Let $\alpha=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{5}{12}$, so $\cos\alpha=\dfrac{12}{13}$, $\sin\alpha=\dfrac{5}{13}$ and $\alpha\approx0.39$.
The bracket is $\cos(x-\alpha)$.
For $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\le x\le\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$, $x-\alpha$ lies between about 1.18 and 1.96, inside $[0,\pi]$.
So $\cos^{-1}(\cos(x-\alpha))=x-\tan^{-1}\dfrac{5}{12}$.

questions.text: The value of $(\sin70^\circ)(\cot10^\circ\cot70^\circ-1)$ is
questions.sol:
$\cot10^\circ\cot70^\circ-1=\dfrac{\cos10^\circ\cos70^\circ-\sin10^\circ\sin70^\circ}{\sin10^\circ\sin70^\circ}=\dfrac{\cos80^\circ}{\sin10^\circ\sin70^\circ}$.
Multiplying by $\sin70^\circ$ gives $\dfrac{\cos80^\circ}{\sin10^\circ}=1$.

questions.text: If the line $3x-2y+12=0$ intersects the parabola $4y=3x^2$ at the points A and B, then at the vertex of the parabola, the line segment AB subtends an angle equal to
questions.sol:
Substitute $y=\dfrac{3x+12}{2}$: $2(3x+12)=3x^2 \Rightarrow x^2-2x-8=0$, so $x=4$ or $-2$.
A$(4,12)$, B$(-2,3)$, vertex O$(0,0)$.
$\vec{OA}\cdot\vec{OB}=-8+36=28$ and $|\vec{OA}\times\vec{OB}|=|4\cdot3-12\cdot(-2)|=36$.
$\tan\theta=\dfrac{36}{28}=\dfrac97$, so the angle is $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac97\right)$.

questions.text: Let the arc AC of a circle subtend a right angle at the centre O. If the point B on the arc AC, divides the arc AC such that $\dfrac{\text{length of arc AB}}{\text{length of arc BC}}=\dfrac15$, and $\overrightarrow{OC}=\alpha\overrightarrow{OA}+\beta\overrightarrow{OB}$, then $\alpha+\sqrt2(\sqrt3-1)\beta$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Angle AOB $=15^\circ$ and angle BOC $=75^\circ$.
Take $\overrightarrow{OA}=(1,0)$, $\overrightarrow{OC}=(0,1)$, $\overrightarrow{OB}=(\cos15^\circ,\sin15^\circ)$.
$(0,1)=\alpha(1,0)+\beta(\cos15^\circ,\sin15^\circ)$ gives $\beta=\dfrac{1}{\sin15^\circ}=\dfrac{2\sqrt2}{\sqrt3-1}$ and $\alpha=-\cot15^\circ=-(2+\sqrt3)$.
$\alpha+\sqrt2(\sqrt3-1)\beta=-(2+\sqrt3)+4=2-\sqrt3$.

questions.text: Let the position vectors of the vertices A, B and C of a tetrahedron ABCD be $\hat i+2\hat j+\hat k$, $\hat i+3\hat j-2\hat k$ and $2\hat i+\hat j-\hat k$ respectively. The altitude from the vertex D to the opposite face ABC meets the median line segment through A of the triangle ABC at the point E. If the length of AD is $\dfrac{\sqrt{110}}{3}$ and the volume of the tetrahedron is $\dfrac{\sqrt{805}}{6\sqrt2}$, then the position vector of E is
questions.sol:
$\vec{AB}=(0,1,-3)$, $\vec{AC}=(1,-1,-2)$, $\vec{AB}\times\vec{AC}=(-5,-3,-1)$, so area ABC $=\dfrac{\sqrt{35}}{2}$.
Height $h=\dfrac{3V}{\text{area}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{805}}{\sqrt2\sqrt{35}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{23}{2}}$.
$AE^2=AD^2-h^2=\dfrac{110}{9}-\dfrac{23}{2}=\dfrac{13}{18}$.
Midpoint of BC: M$\left(\dfrac32,2,-\dfrac32\right)$, $\vec{AM}=\left(\dfrac12,0,-\dfrac52\right)$, $AM^2=\dfrac{13}{2}$. So $\dfrac{AE}{AM}=\sqrt{\dfrac{13/18}{13/2}}=\dfrac13$.
E $=A+\dfrac13\vec{AM}=\left(\dfrac76,2,\dfrac16\right)=\dfrac16(7\hat i+12\hat j+\hat k)$.

questions.text: Let P be the foot of the perpendicular from the point Q(10, $-3$, $-1$) on the line $\dfrac{x-3}{7}=\dfrac{y-2}{-1}=\dfrac{z+1}{-2}$. Then the area of the right angled triangle PQR, where R is the point (3, $-2$, 1), is
questions.sol:
A point of the line is $(3+7t,\,2-t,\,-1-2t)$. $\vec{QP}=(7t-7,\,5-t,\,-2t)$ must be perpendicular to $(7,-1,-2)$: $54t-54=0$, so $t=1$ and P $=(10,1,-3)$.
$\vec{QR}=(-7,1,2)$ is parallel to the line, so $\vec{QP}\perp\vec{QR}$ and the right angle is at Q.
$|QP|=\sqrt{0+16+4}=\sqrt{20}$, $|QR|=\sqrt{49+1+4}=\sqrt{54}$.
Area $=\dfrac12\sqrt{20\times54}=\dfrac12\sqrt{1080}=3\sqrt{30}$.

questions.text:
If the function
$f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{2}{x}\{\sin(k_1+1)x+\sin(k_2-1)x\}, & x<0\\ 4, & x=0\\ \dfrac{2}{x}\log_e\left(\dfrac{2+k_1x}{2+k_2x}\right), & x>0\end{cases}$
is continuous at $x=0$, then $k_1^2+k_2^2$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Left limit: $2\left((k_1+1)+(k_2-1)\right)=2(k_1+k_2)=4$, so $k_1+k_2=2$.
Right limit: $\dfrac{2}{x}\left[\log_e\left(1+\dfrac{k_1x}{2}\right)-\log_e\left(1+\dfrac{k_2x}{2}\right)\right]\to k_1-k_2=4$.
So $k_1=3$, $k_2=-1$ and $k_1^2+k_2^2=10$.

questions.text: Marks obtains by all the students of class 12 are presented in a freqency distribution with classes of equal width. Let the median of this grouped data be 14 with median class interval 12-18 and median class frequency 12. If the number of students whose marks are less than 12 is 18, then the total number of students is
questions.sol:
Median $=l+\dfrac{\frac N2-cf}{f}\times h$ with $l=12$, $h=6$, $f=12$, $cf=18$.
$14=12+\dfrac{\frac N2-18}{12}\times6 \Rightarrow \dfrac N2-18=4 \Rightarrow N=44$.

questions.text: Let $I(x)=\displaystyle\int\frac{dx}{(x-11)^{\frac{11}{13}}(x+15)^{\frac{15}{13}}}$. If $I(37)-I(24)=\dfrac14\left(\dfrac{1}{b^{\frac{1}{13}}}-\dfrac{1}{c^{\frac{1}{13}}}\right)$, $b,c\in\mathbb{N}$, then $3(b+c)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Write the integrand as $\left(\dfrac{x-11}{x+15}\right)^{-\frac{11}{13}}\dfrac{1}{(x+15)^2}$ and put $t=\dfrac{x-11}{x+15}$, $dt=\dfrac{26}{(x+15)^2}dx$.
$I=\dfrac{1}{26}\displaystyle\int t^{-\frac{11}{13}}dt=\dfrac{1}{26}\cdot\dfrac{13}{2}t^{\frac{2}{13}}=\dfrac14\left(\dfrac{x-11}{x+15}\right)^{\frac{2}{13}}+C$.
$I(37)-I(24)=\dfrac14\left[\left(\dfrac12\right)^{\frac{2}{13}}-\left(\dfrac13\right)^{\frac{2}{13}}\right]=\dfrac14\left(\dfrac{1}{4^{\frac{1}{13}}}-\dfrac{1}{9^{\frac{1}{13}}}\right)$.
$b=4$, $c=9$, so $3(b+c)=39$.

questions.text: The value of $\displaystyle\int_{e^2}^{e^4}\frac1x\left(\frac{e^{\left((\log_e x)^2+1\right)^{-1}}}{e^{\left((\log_e x)^2+1\right)^{-1}}+e^{\left((6-\log_e x)^2+1\right)^{-1}}}\right)dx$ is
questions.sol:
Put $t=\log_e x$, $dt=\dfrac{dx}{x}$; the limits become 2 and 4:
$I=\displaystyle\int_2^4\frac{e^{1/(t^2+1)}}{e^{1/(t^2+1)}+e^{1/((6-t)^2+1)}}dt$.
Replacing $t$ by $6-t$ swaps the two exponentials, so adding the two forms gives $2I=\displaystyle\int_2^4 1\,dt=2$.
$I=1$.

questions.text: Let a curve $y=f(x)$ pass through the points $(0,5)$ and $(\log_e2,k)$. If the curve satisfies the differential equation $2(3+y)e^{2x}dx-(7+e^{2x})dy=0$, then $k$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Separate: $\dfrac{dy}{3+y}=\dfrac{2e^{2x}}{7+e^{2x}}dx \Rightarrow \log_e(3+y)=\log_e(7+e^{2x})+C$.
At $(0,5)$: $\log_e8=\log_e8+C$, so $C=0$ and $3+y=7+e^{2x}$.
At $x=\log_e2$: $3+k=7+4$, so $k=8$.

questions.text: If the equation $a(b-c)x^2+b(c-a)x+c(a-b)=0$ has equal roots, where $a+c=15$ and $b=\dfrac{36}{5}$, then $a^2+c^2$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
The coefficients add to 0, so $x=1$ is a root; with equal roots both roots are 1.
Product of roots: $\dfrac{c(a-b)}{a(b-c)}=1 \Rightarrow ca-bc=ab-ac \Rightarrow b=\dfrac{2ac}{a+c}$.
$\dfrac{36}{5}=\dfrac{2ac}{15} \Rightarrow ac=54$.
$a^2+c^2=(a+c)^2-2ac=225-108=117$.

questions.text: If the area of the larger portion bounded between the curves $x^2+y^2=25$ and $y=|x-1|$ is $\dfrac14(b\pi+c)$, $b,c\in\mathbb{N}$, then $b+c$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
Intersections: for $x\ge1$, $x^2+(x-1)^2=25$ gives $x=4$ (point $(4,3)$); for $x<1$ it gives $x=-3$ (point $(-3,4)$).
Smaller part (above $y=|x-1|$): $\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{4}\sqrt{25-x^2}\,dx-\int_{-3}^{4}|x-1|\,dx$.
$\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{4}\sqrt{25-x^2}\,dx=\left[\frac x2\sqrt{25-x^2}+\frac{25}{2}\sin^{-1}\frac x5\right]_{-3}^{4}=12+\frac{25}{2}\cdot\frac{\pi}{2}=12+\frac{25\pi}{4}$ (since $\sin^{-1}\frac45+\sin^{-1}\frac35=\frac{\pi}{2}$).
$\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{4}|x-1|\,dx=\frac{16}{2}+\frac{9}{2}=\frac{25}{2}$, so the smaller part is $\dfrac{25\pi}{4}-\dfrac12$.
Larger part $=25\pi-\dfrac{25\pi}{4}+\dfrac12=\dfrac14(75\pi+2)$, so $b+c=77$.

questions.text: The sum of all rational terms in the expansion of $\left(1+2^{1/3}+3^{1/2}\right)^6$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
A general term is $\dfrac{6!}{p!\,q!\,r!}\,2^{q/3}\,3^{r/2}$ with $p+q+r=6$; it is rational when $3\mid q$ and $r$ is even.
$q=0$: $r=0,2,4,6$ give $1+15\cdot3+15\cdot9+27=208$.
$q=3$: $r=0$ gives $20\cdot2=40$; $r=2$ gives $60\cdot2\cdot3=360$.
$q=6$: $r=0$ gives $2^2=4$.
Sum $=208+400+4=612$.

questions.text: Let the circle C touch the line $x-y+1=0$, have the centre on the positive x-axis, and cut off a chord of length $\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{13}}$ along the line $-3x+2y=1$. Let H be the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{\alpha^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{\beta^2}=1$, whose one of the foci is the centre of C and the length of the transverse axis is the diameter of C. Then $2\alpha^2+3\beta^2$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
Centre $(h,0)$, $h>0$; tangency gives $r=\dfrac{h+1}{\sqrt2}$.
Distance of the centre from $-3x+2y=1$ is $\dfrac{3h+1}{\sqrt{13}}$, and half the chord is $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{13}}$:
$\dfrac{(h+1)^2}{2}=\dfrac{(3h+1)^2+4}{13} \Rightarrow 5h^2-14h-3=0 \Rightarrow h=3$, so $r=2\sqrt2$.
Hyperbola: $2\alpha=4\sqrt2$, so $\alpha^2=8$; focus at $(3,0)$ gives $\alpha^2+\beta^2=9$, so $\beta^2=1$.
$2\alpha^2+3\beta^2=16+3=19$.

questions.text: If the set of all values of $a$, for which the equation $5x^3-15x-a=0$ has three distinct real roots, is the interval $(\alpha,\beta)$, then $\beta-2\alpha$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
Let $f(x)=5x^3-15x$. $f'(x)=15(x^2-1)=0$ at $x=\pm1$, with $f(-1)=10$ (local maximum) and $f(1)=-10$ (local minimum).
$f(x)=a$ has three distinct real roots when $-10<a<10$.
$\beta-2\alpha=10+20=30$.

questions.text: The position of a particle moving on x-axis is given by $x(t)=A\sin t+B\cos^2t+Ct^2+D$, where $t$ is time. The dimension of $\dfrac{ABC}{D}$ is
questions.sol:
Each term has the dimension of length: $[A]=[B]=[D]=$ L and $[C]t^2=$ L, so $[C]=$ LT$^{-2}$.
$\left[\dfrac{ABC}{D}\right]=\dfrac{\text{L}\cdot\text{L}\cdot\text{LT}^{-2}}{\text{L}}=$ L$^2$T$^{-2}$.

questions.text:
The electric flux is $\phi=\alpha\sigma+\beta\lambda$
where $\lambda$ and $\sigma$ are linear and surface charge density, respectively. $\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta}\right)$ represents
questions.sol:
Both terms have the dimension of flux, so $\alpha\sigma$ and $\beta\lambda$ have the same dimension.
$\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta}=\dfrac{\lambda}{\sigma}$, with units $\dfrac{\text{C m}^{-1}}{\text{C m}^{-2}}=$ m.
So $\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta}$ has the dimension of length: displacement.

questions.text: A solid sphere of mass 'm' and radius 'r' is allowed to roll without slipping from the highest point of an inclined plane of length 'L' and makes an angle $30^\circ$ with the horizontal. The speed of the particle at the bottom of the plane is $v_1$. If the angle of inclination is increased to $45^\circ$ while keeping L constant. Then the new speed of the sphere at the bottom of the plane is $v_2$. The ratio $v_1^2:v_2^2$ is
questions.sol:
For rolling without slipping, $mgh=\dfrac12mv^2\left(1+\dfrac{k^2}{r^2}\right)$, so $v^2\propto h=L\sin\theta$.
$v_1^2:v_2^2=\sin30^\circ:\sin45^\circ=\dfrac12:\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}=1:\sqrt2$.

questions.text: The motion of an airplane is represented by velocity-time graph as shown below. The distance covered by airplane in the first 30.5 second is _____ km.
questions.sol:
Distance is the area under the v-t graph.
From 0 to 2 s (200 to 400 m/s): $\dfrac{200+400}{2}\times2=600$ m.
From 2 s to 30.5 s at 400 m/s: $400\times28.5=11400$ m.
Total $=12000$ m $=12$ km.

questions.text: Consider a circular disc of radius 20 cm with centre located at the origin. A circular hole of radius 5 cm is cut from this disc in such a way that the edge of the hole touches the edge of the disc. The distance of centre of mass of residual or remaining disc from the origin will be
questions.sol:
The hole's centre is $20-5=15$ cm from the origin. Mass is proportional to area: whole disc $400\pi$, hole $25\pi$ (in cm$^2$ units).
$x_{cm}=\dfrac{0-25\times15}{400-25}=-\dfrac{375}{375}=-1$ cm.
The distance from the origin is 1.0 cm (on the side away from the hole).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The hot water flows faster than cold water
Statement II: Soap water has higher surface tension as compared to fresh water.
In the light above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: viscosity of water falls as temperature rises, so hot water flows faster. True.
Statement II: soap lowers the surface tension of water. False.

questions.text:
A gun fires a lead bullet of temperature 300 K into a wooden block. The bullet having melting temperature of 600 K penetrates into the block and melts down. If the total heat required for the process is 625 J, then the mass of the bullet is _____grams.
(Latent heat of fusion of lead $=2.5\times10^4$ JKg$^{-1}$ and specific heat capacity of lead $=125$ JKg$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$)
questions.sol:
Heat to warm from 300 K to 600 K and then melt: $Q=m(c\Delta T+L)=m(125\times300+25000)=62500\,m$.
$62500\,m=625 \Rightarrow m=0.01$ kg $=10$ g.

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
LIST-ILIST-II
A.Pressure varies inversely with volume of an ideal gas.I.Adiabatic process
B.Heat absorbed goes partly to increase internal energy and partly to do work.II.Isochoric process
C.Heat is neither absorbed nor released by a system.III.Isothermal process
D.No work is done on or by a gas.IV.Isobaric process
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: $p\propto\dfrac1V$ is Boyle's law, an isothermal process (III).
B: at constant pressure the heat supplied raises internal energy and also does work $p\Delta V$: isobaric (IV).
C: no heat exchange is adiabatic (I).
D: no work means constant volume, isochoric (II).
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text:
A light hollow cube of side length 10 cm and mass 10g, is floating in water. It is pushed down and released to execute simple harmonic oscillations. The time period of oscillations is $y\pi\times10^{-2}$ s, where the value of $y$ is
(Acceleration due to gravity, $g=10$ m/s$^2$, density of water $=10^3$ kg/m$^3$)
questions.sol:
Pushing the cube down by $x$ adds buoyant force $\rho Agx$, so the restoring constant is $k=\rho Ag=10^3\times0.01\times10=100$ N/m.
$T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac mk}=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{0.01}{100}}=2\pi\times10^{-2}$ s.
$y=2$.

questions.text:
Identify the valid statements relevant to the given circuit at the instant when the key is closed.
A. There will be no current through resistor R.
B. There will be maximum current in the connecting wires.
C. Potential difference between the capacitor plates A and B is minimum.
D. Charge on the capacitor plates is minimum.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
At the instant the key is closed the capacitor is uncharged, so it behaves like a plain wire.
The current is then largest, $\dfrac{5}{R}$, and flows through R, so A is false and B is true.
The charge, and hence the potential difference across the plates, is zero at that instant, i.e. minimum: C and D are true.
B, C, D only.

questions.text: A point particle of charge Q is located at P along the axis of an electric dipole 1 at a distance r as shown in the figure. The point P is also on the equatorial plane of a second electric dipole 2 at a distance r. The dipoles are made of opposite charge q separated by a distance $2a$. For the charge particle at P not to experience any net force, which of the following correctly describes the situation?
questions.sol:
Measuring r from each dipole's centre, the axial field of dipole 1 at P is $\dfrac{kq\cdot4ar}{(r^2-a^2)^2}$ and the equatorial field of dipole 2 is $\dfrac{kq\cdot2a}{(r^2+a^2)^{3/2}}$; from the figure they point in opposite directions.
No net force needs $2r(r^2+a^2)^{3/2}=(r^2-a^2)^2$. With $x=\dfrac ar$: $2(1+x^2)^{3/2}=(1-x^2)^2$.
At $x=3$: left side $2\times10^{3/2}\approx63.2$, right side $64$, so $x\approx3$.
$\dfrac ar\sim3$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Regarding self-inductance:
A. The self-inductance of the coil depends on its geometry.
B. Self-inductance does not depend on the permeability of the medium.
C. Self-induced e.m.f. opposes any change in the current in a circuit.
D. Self-inductance is electromagnetic analogue of mass in mechanics.
E. Work needs to be done against self-induced e.m.f. in establishing the current.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: $L=\mu_0\mu_rn^2Al$ depends on the coil's shape and size. True.
B: $L$ is proportional to the permeability of the core medium. False.
C: Lenz's law. True.
D: inductance opposes changes in current as mass opposes changes in velocity. True.
E: energy $\dfrac12LI^2$ is stored by doing work against the back e.m.f. True.
A, C, D, E only.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Consider a moving coil galvanometer (MCG):
A. The torsional constant in moving coil galvanometer has dimentions [ML$^2$T$^{-2}$]
B. Increasing the current sensitivity may not necessarily increase the voltage sensitivity.
C. If we increase number of turns (N) to its double (2N), then the voltage sensitivity doubles.
D. MCG can be converted into an ammeter by introducing a shunt resistance of large value in parallel with galvanometer.
E. Current sensitivity of MCG depends inversely on number of turns of coil.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: torque $=k\theta$ with $\theta$ dimensionless, so $[k]=$ ML$^2$T$^{-2}$. True.
B: voltage sensitivity $=\dfrac{\text{current sensitivity}}{R}$; raising N raises both the current sensitivity and R. True.
C: doubling N doubles $NAB/k$ but also doubles the coil resistance, so the voltage sensitivity is unchanged. False.
D: an ammeter needs a small shunt. False.
E: current sensitivity $=\dfrac{NAB}{k}$ is proportional to N. False.
A, B only.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The electric field of an electromagnetic wave in free space is
$\vec E=57\cos\left[7.5\times10^6t-5\times10^{-3}(3x+4y)\right]\left(4\hat i-3\hat j\right)$ N/C.
The associated magnetic field in Tesla is
questions.sol:
The phase $\omega t-\vec k\cdot\vec r$ shows propagation along $\hat n=\dfrac{3\hat i+4\hat j}{5}$.
$\vec B=\dfrac1c\,\hat n\times\vec E$, and $\dfrac{(3\hat i+4\hat j)\times(4\hat i-3\hat j)}{5}=\dfrac{-9\hat k-16\hat k}{5}=-5\hat k$.
So $\vec B=-\dfrac{57}{3\times10^8}\cos[\ldots](5\hat k)$; its magnitude $\dfrac{57\times5}{c}$ matches $\dfrac{|\vec E|}{c}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Given a thin convex lens (refractive index $\mu_2$), kept in a liquid (refractive index $\mu_1$, $\mu_1<\mu_2$) having radii of curvatures $|R_1|$ and $|R_2|$. Its second surface is silver polished. Where should an object be placed on the optic axis so that a real and inverted image is formed at the same place?
questions.sol:
The image coincides with the object when the light, after refraction at the first surface, strikes the silvered surface normally, i.e. heads for its centre of curvature, a distance $|R_2|$ in front of the (thin) lens.
Refraction at the first surface (object at distance $x$, sign convention with light travelling left to right): $\dfrac{\mu_2}{-|R_2|}-\dfrac{\mu_1}{-x}=\dfrac{\mu_2-\mu_1}{|R_1|}$.
$\dfrac{\mu_1}{x}=\dfrac{\mu_2-\mu_1}{|R_1|}+\dfrac{\mu_2}{|R_2|}=\dfrac{\mu_2(|R_1|+|R_2|)-\mu_1|R_2|}{|R_1||R_2|}$.
$x=\dfrac{\mu_1|R_1||R_2|}{\mu_2(|R_1|+|R_2|)-\mu_1|R_2|}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: What is the lateral shift of a ray refracted through a parallel-sided glass slab of thickness 'h' in terms of the angle of incidence 'i' and angle of refraction 'r', if the glass slab is placed in air medium?
questions.sol:
Inside the slab the ray travels a distance $\dfrac{h}{\cos r}$.
The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray, displaced sideways by this path length times $\sin(i-r)$.
Lateral shift $=\dfrac{h\sin(i-r)}{\cos r}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A spherical surface of radius of curvature R, separates air from glass (refractive index = 1.5). The centre of curvature is in the glass medium. A point object 'O' placed in air on the optic axis of the surface, so that its real image is formed at 'I' inside glass. The line OI intersects the spherical surface at P and PO = PI. The distance PO equals to
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{\mu_2}{v}-\dfrac{\mu_1}{u}=\dfrac{\mu_2-\mu_1}{R}$ with $u=-x$, $v=+x$, $\mu_1=1$, $\mu_2=1.5$:
$\dfrac{1.5}{x}+\dfrac1x=\dfrac{0.5}{R} \Rightarrow x=5R$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A sub-atomic particle of mass $10^{-30}$ kg is moving with a velocity $2.21\times10^6$ m/s. Under the matter wave consideration, the particle will behave closely like _____.
($h=6.63\times10^{-34}$ J.s)
questions.sol:
de Broglie wavelength: $\lambda=\dfrac{h}{mv}=\dfrac{6.63\times10^{-34}}{10^{-30}\times2.21\times10^6}=3\times10^{-10}$ m $=0.3$ nm.
This lies in the X-ray region.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: A radioactive nucleus $n_2$ has 3 times the decay constant as compared to the decay constant of another radioactive nucleus $n_1$. If initial number of both nuclei are the same, what is the ratio of number of nuclei of $n_2$ to the number of nuclei of $n_1$, after one half-life of $n_1$?
questions.sol:
After one half-life of $n_1$, $N_1=\dfrac{N_0}{2}$.
$n_2$ decays three times as fast, so in the same time it passes through three of its own half-lives: $N_2=\dfrac{N_0}{8}$.
$\dfrac{N_2}{N_1}=\dfrac14$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Refer to the circuit diagram given in the figure. which of the following observations are correct?
A. Total resistance of circuit is 6 $\Omega$
B. Current in Ammeter is 1A
C. Potential across AB is 4 Volts.
D. Potential across CD is 4 Volts
E. Total resistance of the circuit is 8 $\Omega$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Taking the diode as ideal and conducting, the two lower 4 $\Omega$ resistors (D to the bottom rail, and A to B) are in parallel: 2 $\Omega$.
Total resistance $=4+2=6$ $\Omega$ (A true, E false); current $=\dfrac{6}{6}=1$ A (B true).
$V_{CD}=1\times4=4$ V (D true); $V_{AB}=1\times2=2$ V (C false).
A, B and D only.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two particles are located at equal distance from origin. The position vectors of those are represented by $\vec A=2\hat i+3n\hat j+2\hat k$ and $\vec B=2\hat i-2\hat j+4p\hat k$, respectively. If both the vectors are at right angle to each other, the value of $n^{-1}$ is _____.
questions.sol:
Equal magnitudes: $4+9n^2+4=4+4+16p^2 \Rightarrow 9n^2=16p^2$.
Perpendicular: $4-6n+8p=0 \Rightarrow 4p=3n-2$.
So $9n^2=(3n-2)^2 \Rightarrow 12n=4 \Rightarrow n=\dfrac13$.
$n^{-1}=3$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A force $\vec f=x^2y\hat i+y^2\hat j$ acts on a particle in a plane $x+y=10$. The work done by this force during a displacement from $(0,0)$ to $(4\text{m},2\text{m})$ is _____ Joule (round off to the nearest integer)
questions.note: As printed the data do not fit together: $(0,0)$ and $(4,2)$ do not lie on $x+y=10$, and the force is not conservative, so the work depends on the path. The official answer 152 comes from putting $y=10-x$ in the $x$-component only, as shown in the solution; along the straight line from $(0,0)$ to $(4,2)$ the work would be about 35 J.
questions.sol:
Following the intended method, use $x+y=10$ to write $f_x=x^2(10-x)$ and integrate each component over its own range.
$W=\displaystyle\int_0^4x^2(10-x)\,dx+\int_0^2y^2\,dy=\left(\frac{640}{3}-64\right)+\frac83=\frac{448}{3}+\frac83=152$ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An ideal gas initially at $0^\circ$C temperature, is compressed suddenly to one fourth of its volume. If the ratio of specific heat at constant pressure to that at constant volume is 3/2, the change in temperature due to the thermodynamic process is _____ K.
questions.sol:
A sudden compression is adiabatic: $TV^{\gamma-1}=$ constant.
$T_2=T_1\left(\dfrac{V_1}{V_2}\right)^{\gamma-1}=273\times4^{1/2}=546$ K.
Change in temperature $=546-273=273$ K.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In the given circuit the sliding contact is pulled outwards such that electric current in the circuit changes at the rate of 8 A/s. At an instant when R is 12 $\Omega$, the value of the current in the circuit will be _____ A.
questions.sol:
Pulling the contact outwards increases R, so the current falls: $\dfrac{dI}{dt}=-8$ A/s.
$E-L\dfrac{dI}{dt}=IR \Rightarrow 12+3\times8=12I$.
$I=3$ A.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A positive ion A and a negative ion B has charges $6.67\times10^{-19}$ C and $9.6\times10^{-10}$ C, and masses $19.2\times10^{-27}$ kg and $9\times10^{-27}$ kg respectively. At an instant, the ions are separated by a certain distance r. At that instant the ratio of the magnitudes of electrostatic force to gravitational force is $P\times10^{-13}$, where the value of P is ______.
(Take $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}=9\times10^9$ Nm$^2$C$^{-1}$ and universal gravitational constant as $6.67\times10^{-11}$ Nm$^2$ kg$^{-2}$)
questions.note: Dropped in the official final key: full marks to everyone. With the data as printed the ratio is about $5\times10^{44}$, nowhere near the form $P\times10^{-13}$, so no sensible value of P exists. The answer shown (0) is only a placeholder.
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{F_e}{F_g}=\dfrac{kq_1q_2}{Gm_1m_2}$ (the distance cancels).
$=\dfrac{9\times10^9\times6.67\times10^{-19}\times9.6\times10^{-10}}{6.67\times10^{-11}\times19.2\times10^{-27}\times9\times10^{-27}}=\dfrac{8.64\times10^{-19}}{1.728\times10^{-63}}=5\times10^{44}$.
This cannot be written as $P\times10^{-13}$ with a reasonable P, so the question has no valid answer as set.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
$2.8\times10^{-3}$ mol of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ is left after removing $10^{21}$ molecules from its '$x$' mg sample. The mass of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ taken initially is
Given: $N_A=6.02\times10^{23}$ mol$^{-1}$
questions.sol:
Moles removed $=\dfrac{10^{21}}{6.02\times10^{23}}=1.66\times10^{-3}$ mol.
Initial moles $=2.8\times10^{-3}+1.66\times10^{-3}=4.46\times10^{-3}$ mol.
Mass $=4.46\times10^{-3}\times44$ g $\approx0.196$ g $=196.2$ mg.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Heat treatment of muscular pain involves radiation of wavelength of about 900 nm. Which spectral line of H atom is suitable for this?
Given : Rydberg constant $R_H=10^5$ cm$^{-1}$, $h=6.6\times10^{-34}$ J s, $c=3\times10^8$ m/s)
questions.sol:
$\dfrac1\lambda=\dfrac{1}{900\times10^{-7}\text{ cm}}=1.11\times10^4$ cm$^{-1}$.
$R_H\left(\dfrac{1}{n_1^2}-\dfrac{1}{n_2^2}\right)=1.11\times10^4 \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{n_1^2}-\dfrac{1}{n_2^2}=\dfrac19$.
This is $n_1=3$, $n_2=\infty$: the Paschen series limit, $\infty\to3$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
LIST-I
(Classification of molecules based on octet rule)		LIST-II
(Example)
A.Molecules obeying octet ruleI.NO, $\mathrm{NO_2}$
B.Molecules with incomplete octetII.$\mathrm{BCl_3}$, $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$
C.Molecules with incomplete octet with odd electronIII.$\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$, $\mathrm{PCl_5}$
D.Molecules with expanded octetIV.$\mathrm{CCl_4}$, $\mathrm{CO_2}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: $\mathrm{CCl_4}$ and $\mathrm{CO_2}$ obey the octet rule (IV).
B: B and Al in $\mathrm{BCl_3}$, $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ have only 6 electrons (II).
C: NO and $\mathrm{NO_2}$ are odd-electron molecules (I).
D: S in $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ and P in $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ have expanded octets (III).
A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Ice at $-5^\circ$C is heated to become vapor with temperature of $110^\circ$C at atmospheric pressure. The entropy change associated with this process can be obtained from
questions.sol:
Entropy is added up stage by stage, with $dS=\dfrac{dq_{\text{rev}}}{T}$.
Heating ice from 268 K to 273 K: $\displaystyle\int\frac{C_{p,\text{m}}}{T}dT$; melting at $T_f=273$ K: $\dfrac{\Delta H_{\text{fus}}}{T_f}$; heating water from 273 K to 373 K: $\displaystyle\int\frac{C_{p,\text{m}}}{T}dT$; boiling at $T_b=373$ K: $\dfrac{\Delta H_{\text{vap}}}{T_b}$; heating vapour from 373 K to 383 K: $\displaystyle\int\frac{C_{p,\text{m}}}{T}dT$.
Only one option divides every heating term by $T$ and every phase change by its transition temperature; the others use $\int C_p\,dT$, which is a heat, not an entropy.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
$\mathrm{CrCl_3.xNH_3}$ can exist as a complex. 0.1 molal aqueous solution of this complex shows a depression in freezing point of $0.558^\circ$C. Assuming 100% ionisation of this complex and coordination number of Cr is 6, the complex will be
(Given $K_f=1.86$ K kg mol$^{-1}$)
questions.sol:
$\Delta T_f=iK_fm \Rightarrow 0.558=i\times1.86\times0.1 \Rightarrow i=3$.
Three ions per formula unit: one complex cation and two chloride ions.
With coordination number 6 this is $\mathrm{[Cr(NH_3)_5Cl]Cl_2}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Which of the following happens when $\mathrm{NH_4OH}$ is added gradually to the solution containing 1M $\mathrm{A^{2+}}$ and 1M $\mathrm{B^{3+}}$ ions?
Given : $K_{sp}[\mathrm{A(OH)_2}]=9\times10^{-10}$ and $K_{sp}[\mathrm{B(OH)_3}]=27\times10^{-18}$ at 298 K.
options: Both $\mathrm{A(OH)_2}$ and $\mathrm{B(OH)_3}$ do not show precipitation with $\mathrm{NH_4OH}$
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{A(OH)_2}$ starts to precipitate when $[\mathrm{OH^-}]^2=9\times10^{-10}$, i.e. $[\mathrm{OH^-}]=3\times10^{-5}$ M.
$\mathrm{B(OH)_3}$ starts when $[\mathrm{OH^-}]^3=27\times10^{-18}$, i.e. $[\mathrm{OH^-}]=3\times10^{-6}$ M.
$\mathrm{B(OH)_3}$ needs the smaller hydroxide concentration, so it precipitates first.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
$\mathrm{FeO_4^{2-}\xrightarrow{+2.0\,V}Fe^{3+}\xrightarrow{0.8\,V}Fe^{2+}\xrightarrow{-0.5\,V}Fe^0}$
In the above diagram, the standard electrode potentials are given in volts (over the arrow).
The value of $E^\ominus_{\mathrm{FeO_4^{2-}/Fe^{2+}}}$ is
questions.sol:
Add free energies, $\Delta G^\ominus=-nFE^\ominus$.
$\mathrm{FeO_4^{2-}\to Fe^{3+}}$: $n=3$ (Fe +6 to +3), $3\times2.0=6.0$. $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}\to Fe^{2+}}$: $n=1$, $1\times0.8=0.8$.
$E^\ominus_{\mathrm{FeO_4^{2-}/Fe^{2+}}}=\dfrac{6.0+0.8}{4}=1.7$ V.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The element that does not belong to the same period of the remaining elements (modern periodic table) is:
questions.sol:
Os (76), Ir (77) and Pt (78) are 5d elements in period 6.
Pd (46) is a 4d element in period 5.

questions.text: The incorrect statement among the following is
options: $\mathrm{SO_2}$ can act as an oxidizing agent, but not as a reducing agent.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{PH_3}$ is a weaker base than $\mathrm{NH_3}$ (lower proton affinity): correct.
N has no d orbitals and cannot expand its octet, so $\mathrm{NF_5}$ does not exist while $\mathrm{PF_3}$ does: correct.
$\mathrm{NO_2}$ is an odd-electron molecule and dimerises to $\mathrm{N_2O_4}$: correct.
S in $\mathrm{SO_2}$ is +4, between $-2$ and $+6$, so $\mathrm{SO_2}$ acts as both an oxidising and a reducing agent. The last statement is incorrect.

questions.text: The correct set of ions (aqueous solution) with same colour from the following is:
questions.sol:
Colours of the aqua ions (NCERT table): $\mathrm{V^{2+}}$ violet, $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$ violet, $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$ violet.
The other sets mix colours: $\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{Ti^{4+}}$ and $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$ are colourless, $\mathrm{Ti^{3+}}$ purple, $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$ blue, $\mathrm{V^{4+}}$ blue, $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$ pink, $\mathrm{V^{3+}}$ green, $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ yellow.

questions.text: The d$-$ electronic configuration of an octahedral Co(II) complex having magnetic moment of 3.95 BM is:
questions.sol:
$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$: 3.95 BM is close to $\sqrt{15}=3.87$ BM, so $n=3$ unpaired electrons.
Co(II) is $\mathrm{d^7}$; in an octahedral field three unpaired electrons means high spin: $t_{2g}^5e_g^2$.
($e^4t_2^3$ is tetrahedral notation, and $t_{2g}^6e_g^1$ has one unpaired electron.)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The complex that shows Facial - Meridional isomerism is:
questions.sol:
Fac-mer isomerism occurs in octahedral complexes of the type $\mathrm{[MA_3B_3]}$.
$\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_3Cl_3]}$ is of this type. $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]^+}$ and $\mathrm{[Co(en)_2Cl_2]^+}$ show cis-trans isomerism, and $\mathrm{[Co(en)_3]^{3+}}$ shows optical isomerism.

questions.text: Propane molecule on chlorination under photochemical condition gives two di-chloro products, "x" and "y". Amongst "x" and "y", "x" is an optically active molecule. How many tri-chloro products (consider only structural isomers) will be obtained from "x" when it is further treated with chlorine under the photochemical condition?
questions.sol:
The optically active dichloropropane is 1,2-dichloropropane, $\mathrm{CH_2Cl{-}CHCl{-}CH_3}$ (C2 is chiral).
Replacing one more H: at C1 gives 1,1,2-trichloropropane; at C2 gives 1,2,2-trichloropropane; at C3 gives 1,2,3-trichloropropane.
So 3 structural isomers.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The correct stability order of the following species/molecules is:
questions.sol:
q, the cyclopentadienyl anion, is planar and cyclic with $6\pi$ electrons: aromatic, most stable.
r, cyclo-octatetraene, takes a non-planar tub shape and is non-aromatic.
p, the cyclopropenyl anion, would have $4\pi$ electrons: antiaromatic, least stable.
Order: q > r > p.

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
LIST-I
Name reaction		LIST-II
Product obtainable
A.Swarts reactionI.Ethyl benzene
B.Sandmeyer's reactionII.Ethyl iodide
C.Wurtz Fittig reactionIII.Cyanobenzene

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

questions.text:
What amount of bromine will be required to convert 2 g of phenol into 2,4,6-tribromophenol?
(Given molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ of C, H, O, Br are 12, 1, 16, 80 respectively )
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{C_6H_5OH+3Br_2\to C_6H_2Br_3OH+3HBr}$.
Phenol: $\dfrac{2}{94}=0.0213$ mol, so $\mathrm{Br_2}$ needed $=3\times0.0213=0.0638$ mol.
Mass $=0.0638\times160\approx10.21$ g, i.e. 10.22 g.

questions.text:
The major product of the following reaction is:
$\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH{=}O\xrightarrow[\text{reflux}]{\text{excess HCHO, alkali}}\,?}$
questions.sol:
Propanal has two $\alpha$-hydrogens. With excess HCHO in alkali, two crossed aldol additions put two $\mathrm{CH_2OH}$ groups on the $\alpha$-carbon: $\mathrm{CH_3C(CH_2OH)_2CHO}$.
This aldehyde has no $\alpha$-hydrogen left, so a crossed Cannizzaro reaction with HCHO reduces it to $\mathrm{CH_3C(CH_2OH)_3}$ (HCHO is oxidised to formate).
The product is the triol $\mathrm{CH_3{-}C(CH_2OH)_3}$.

questions.text:
Which among the following react with Hinsberg's reagent?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Hinsberg's reagent (benzenesulphonyl chloride) reacts with primary and secondary amines, which have an N-H bond; tertiary amines do not react.
A (aniline) and C (methylamine) are primary and E (diphenylamine) is secondary, so they react; B (N,N-dimethylaniline) and D (trimethylamine) are tertiary.
A, C and E only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Fructose does not contain an aldehydic group but still reduces Tollen's reagent
Statement II: In the presence of base, fructose undergoes rearrangement to give glucose.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Fructose is a ketose, yet it reduces Tollens' reagent. True.
The reason is that in the alkaline reagent fructose isomerises (through an enediol) to glucose and mannose, which are aldoses. True.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In Lassaigne's test, the covalent organic molecules are transformed into ionic compounds.
Statement II: The sodium fusion extract of an organic compound having N and S gives prussian blue colour with $\mathrm{FeSO_4}$ and $\mathrm{Na_4[Fe(CN)_6]}$
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: fusion with sodium converts covalently bound N, S and halogens into ionic NaCN, $\mathrm{Na_2S}$, NaX. True.
Statement II: when both N and S are present, sodium thiocyanate forms and gives a blood-red colour with $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$, not Prussian blue; nor is Prussian blue made by adding $\mathrm{Na_4[Fe(CN)_6]}$. False.

questions.text: The standard enthalpy and standard entropy of decomposition of $\mathrm{N_2O_4}$ to $\mathrm{NO_2}$ are 55.0 kJ mol$^{-1}$ and 175.0 J/K/mol respectively. The standard free energy change for this reaction at $25^\circ$C in J mol$^{-1}$ is _____ (Nearest integer)
questions.sol: $\Delta G^\ominus=\Delta H^\ominus-T\Delta S^\ominus=55000-298\times175.0=55000-52150=2850$ J mol$^{-1}$.

If 1 mM solution of ethylamine produces pH = 9, then the ionization constant ($K_b$) of ethylamine is $10^{-x}$. The value of $x$ is _____ (nearest integer).

questions.text:
For the thermal decomposition of $\mathrm{N_2O_5(g)}$ at constant volume, the following table can be formed, for the reaction mentioned below.
$\mathrm{2N_2O_5(g)\to2N_2O_4(g)+O_2(g)}$
Sr.NoTime/sTotal pressure/(atm)
100.6
2100'x'
$x=$ ______ $\times10^{-3}$ atm [nearest integer]
Given : Rate constant for the reaction is $4.606\times10^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$.
questions.sol:
First order (units s$^{-1}$): $kt=4.606\times10^{-2}\times100=4.606=2.303\log\dfrac{p_0}{p}$, so $\dfrac{p_0}{p}=100$.
$p_{\mathrm{N_2O_5}}=\dfrac{0.6}{100}=0.006$ atm, so 0.594 atm has decomposed.
This gives 0.594 atm of $\mathrm{N_2O_4}$ and 0.297 atm of $\mathrm{O_2}$.
Total $=0.006+0.594+0.297=0.897$ atm $=897\times10^{-3}$ atm.

questions.text:
Consider the following sequence of reactions to produce major product (A)
Molar mass of product (A) is _____ g mol$^{-1}$.
(Given molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ of C : 12, H: 1, O :16, Br : 80, N : 14, P:31)
questions.sol:
i) $\mathrm{Br_2}$/Fe brominates the ring of 3-nitrotoluene.
ii) Sn/HCl reduces $\mathrm{-NO_2}$ to $\mathrm{-NH_2}$.
iii) $\mathrm{NaNO_2}$/HCl at 273 K gives the diazonium salt.
iv) $\mathrm{H_3PO_2}$ replaces $\mathrm{-N_2^+}$ by H.
The product A is a bromotoluene, $\mathrm{C_7H_7Br}$, whichever ring position the bromine takes.
Molar mass $=7(12)+7(1)+80=171$ g mol$^{-1}$.

questions.text:
During "S" estimation, 160 mg of an organic compound gives 466 mg of barium sulphate. The percentage of Sulphur in the given compound is ______%.
(Given molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ of Ba : 137, S : 32, O : 16)
questions.sol:
Molar mass of $\mathrm{BaSO_4}=233$ g mol$^{-1}$, so mass of S $=\dfrac{32}{233}\times466=64$ mg.
Percentage of S $=\dfrac{64}{160}\times100=40$%.
